newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR HALF-CENTURY HALTS INDIA'S SLIDE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR HALF-CENTURY HALTS INDIA'S SLIDE.

text.p: Captain Sachin Tendulkar hit his 19th test half-century to halt an early slide as India went to tea at 120 for three on the second day of the second and final test against Sri Lanka on Sunday.
India, replying to Sri Lanka's first innings total of 332, suffered early blows as they lost opener Ajay Jadeja and Rahul Dravid on a pitch helping the seamers.
Tendulkar was fortunate to be still batting at tea, after being dropped by his counterpart Arjuna Ranatunga when on 34.
The unlucky bowler was Ravindra Pushpakumara, who saw his captain drop a catch low to his left at first slip.
Sri Lanka, having reduced India to 39 for two at lunch, were restricted to a solitary success in the afternoon session.
That was the wicket of Navjot Sidhu, who lost patience against off-spinner Muthiah Muralitharan and was stumped by Romesh Kaluwitharana for 29 as he jumped out to drive.
Tendulkar, driving crisply on both sides of the wicket, reached his half-century off 60 balls in 94 minutes with seven fours.
At tea he was undefeated on 62 with Mohammad Azharuddin on 22.
